description.value: VBM study of gray matter volume differences across clinically defined ALS phenotypes using routine 1.5T structural MRI.

spans.text: We therefore aimed to examine whether ALS patients with distinct clinical and cMRI phenotypes display subgroup-specific brain tissue volume changes, as revealed by VBM analysis.

value: We hypothesized that GM volume would be more reduced in cortical (extramotor and possibly motor) regions of ALS-FTD patients, in line with previous pathologic studies; and, alternatively, that ALS patients with predominantly UMN or those with mixed UMN plus prominent LMN dysfunction (classic ALS) would have less GM volume loss if subcortical white matter tracts were mostly affected.
